svg.title: Lamport's mutex: A crashes, and no one enters again
svg.desc: Timelines for A, B, C. request on B: L 1; queue (1,B); heard A:0 C:0; holds no. request on C: L 1; queue (1,C); heard A:0 B:0; holds no. request on A: L 1; queue (1,A); heard B:0 C:0; holds no. crash on A. req from A on B, receiving req 1 from request on A: L 3; queue (1,A) (1,B); heard A:1 C:0; holds no. req from A on C, receiving req 1 from request on A: L 3; queue (1,A) (1,C); heard A:1 B:0; holds no. req from C on B, receiving req 1 from request on C: L 5; queue (1,A) (1,B) (1,C); heard A:1 C:1; holds no. req from B on C, receiving req 1 from request on B: L 5; queue (1,A) (1,B) (1,C); heard A:1 B:1; holds no. ack from C on B, receiving ack 5 from req from B on C: L 6; queue (1,A) (1,B) (1,C); heard A:1 C:5; holds no. ack from B on C, receiving ack 5 from req from C on B: L 6; queue (1,A) (1,B) (1,C); heard A:1 B:5; holds no. Note 1: A crashes holding the earliest request, (1,A). Everything sent to it afterwards, B's and C's requests and their acks, goes nowhere. Note 2: B and C have each heard from the other past their own requests, but (1,A) heads both queues, and only A can release it: neither ever enters.

g.text: 1. A crashes holding the earliest request, (1,A). Everything sent to it afterwards, B's and C's requests and their acks, goes nowhere
2. B and C have each heard from the other past their own requests, but (1,A) heads both queues, and only A can release it: neither ever
